page: Vultr vcg-a40-4c-20g-8vram is a fractional GPU instance within the Cloud GPU family. It features an Intel x86_64 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. System memory consists of 20.0 GB of RAM, providing 5.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a 360 GB NVMe SSD. The primary accelerator is a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU, representing approximately 0.1667 of a full GPU, which delivers 8 GB of dedicated VRAM.

Benchmark results show strong performance in specific workloads, particularly in machine learning inference. The instance achieves top-tier results for LLM inference using small and medium models, processing 9881.81 tokens per second for a 135M model prompt and 3161.22 tokens per second for a 7B model prompt. Text generation speeds reach 465.27 tokens per second for the 135M model and 107.91 tokens per second for the 7B model. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks fall mostly in the average range, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1785.29 and a multi-core score of 7057.24. However, certain operations show limitations, such as a weak PassMark database score of 1916.13 and a weak static web serving throughput of 5.81 GB/sec.

By utilizing a fractional GPU allocation, this instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without the expense of a full dedicated accelerator. The combination of 8 GB VRAM, 20.0 GB of system RAM, and a 360 GB NVMe SSD makes it highly suitable for small to medium LLM inference, lightweight machine learning model development, and data processing tasks. It is less optimal for heavy database operations or high-throughput web serving due to the observed performance bottlenecks in those areas.

Acceleration is provided by a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU, which supplies 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates top-tier performance in LLM inference, processing 3161.22 tokens per second for 7B model prompts and 107.91 tokens per second for text generation. General CPU and memory performance remain average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 7057.24, while database operations and web serving throughput are relatively weak. This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for deploying small to medium machine learning models, running inference pipelines, and executing GPU-assisted data processing tasks where a full dedicated GPU is not required.
